comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Scope ruling: this is INFORMATIONAL, not a blocker

Operator ruling received after this ticket was filed: LLMs are non-deterministic, and comparing
two MODELS against one another is out of scope for epic 061c. The epic's scope is that the same
PAYLOADS reach the LLM and the same TOOLS are available, regardless of model and provider.
Ticket 0d76's acceptance criteria are retargeted accordingly — verdict agreement, decision flips,
recall and false-accept are now recorded as INFORMATIONAL evidence, not pass/fail.

So the claim in this ticket's description that the gold-blind flip criterion "is now the sole
remaining blocker on the Bedrock parity slots" is SUPERSEDED. There is no blocker; the remaining
frontier agreement shortfall (0.929) and the three decision flips are the expected outcome of
comparing two different models, not a defect.

What survives, and is why this ticket is left open rather than withdrawn: the observation about
the METRIC itself is independent of the Bedrock decision. `parity_report` computes
`decision_flips` and `verdict_agreement` symmetrically between the two arms and never consults
the gold `label`, even on a gold-labelled corpus where recall and false-accept in the same
function do consult it. Whoever next uses this bar for a genuine A/B of one implementation
against another — the LangGraph -> pydantic-ai cutover it was written for, where both arms ARE
the same model — inherits a criterion that cannot tell an improvement from a regression. That is
the same class of defect as 62ac, and it is worth deciding deliberately.

No root-cause investigation of the specific model differences was performed, and none is
authorised: that question has been ruled irrelevant.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Operator-ratified decision (2026-08-04) — recorded before implementation

Gold-aware ASYMMETRIC scoring for the parity bar's criterion (b): on an arm
disagreement over a gold-labelled item, consult the gold label. A candidate
must NEVER be failed for agreeing with gold against the baseline.

Concretely:
- A decision flip where the CANDIDATE matches gold and the baseline does not
  is a gold-IMPROVING flip — it must not count against the zero-flip gate.
- A flip where the candidate moves AWAY from gold (baseline matched gold, or
  neither matches but candidate diverges from gold) remains a gating failure
  as before.
- Agreement cases are unchanged.
- Missing/absent gold label: behaviour preserved (non-gold pairs were never
  in the flip count; the agreement floor treatment is decided during
  implementation and documented).

Hard constraint: validation via unit tests over recorded/fixture verdicts
only — zero live LLM calls; no full eval sweeps.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## RCA + fix (Gerrit change 1368)

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by RED tests over synthetic fixture records — zero LLM calls):
`parity_report` in `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` computed criterion (b) gold-blind:
- `agreement = _rate(pairs, p[0].decision == p[1].decision)` — symmetric over all pairs
- `decision_flips` — counted every live gold-pair disagreement, selecting on `a.label`
  but never comparing either arm TO the label.
Recall/false-accept in the same function do consult `label`, so the direction of a
disagreement was known and discarded. Result: a candidate correcting a baseline mistake
on a gold item scored as a gating flip (and dragged agreement below 0.95).

FIX (per the operator-ratified 2026-08-04 decision): gold-aware asymmetric scoring.
A disagreement where the candidate genuinely (not errored) matches the gold label is a
gold-IMPROVING flip: reported via the new `gold_improving_flips` metric, exempt from the
zero-flip gate AND the agreement floor. Preserved behaviour: flips AWAY from gold gate as
before; a disagreement where NEITHER arm matches gold still gates (candidate is not
agreeing with gold — documented choice); non-gold (label-less) disagreements still count
symmetrically against the agreement floor and are never flips; errored-pair exclusion
unchanged; an errored candidate side earns no forgiveness.

TESTS (RED first, seen failing pre-fix; mutation check re-seeded the gold-blind
comparison and returned them to RED): 6 new behavioural tests in
tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py (toward-gold not penalized; toward vs away scored
differently; both-wrong still gates; improving disagreements don't trip the agreement
floor; non-gold disagreement earns no forgiveness; errored candidate earns no
forgiveness).

OFFLINE RE-SCORE of the recorded live run (`recheck_recorded`, zero model calls),
per-slot verdicts now recorded in `provider_parity_results.json`:
- standard: PASSED — decision_flips 0, gold_improving_flips 1, agreement 1.0
- frontier: PASSED — decision_flips 0, gold_improving_flips 2, agreement 1.0
All 3 previously-gating flips confirmed gold-improving (candidate matched gold).

Validation: tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py + test_provider_parity.py +
test_fidelity_spot_eval.py all green (65 passed); make lint + make typecheck exit 0.
No live eval runs were performed.

compiled_state.description:
# The parity flip/agreement criteria are gold-blind, so a candidate is failed for being MORE accurate

## Context / Problem

Criterion (b) of the parity bar has two parts, and BOTH compare the two arms to each other
without ever consulting the gold label that the same corpus carries:

* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — `agreement = _rate(pairs, lambda p: p[0].decision == p[1].decision)`
* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — `decision_flips = ... a.decision != b.decision` (gold pairs are
  selected on `a.label`, but the label is never used in the COMPARISON)

Recall and false-accept in the same function DO consult `label`. So the bar already knows which
arm is right on every gold item, and criterion (b) deliberately throws that away.

Consequence, measured on the recorded live Bedrock run
(`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`, re-scored offline with zero model
calls after the 62ac false-accept fix): all THREE decision flips across both slots are cases
where the CANDIDATE (Bedrock) matches gold and the BASELINE (direct Anthropic) does not.

| slot | case | spec | gold | v1 Anthropic | v2 Bedrock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| standard | R-drop-column-no-backfill | code-review-db-migrations | block | advisory | **block** |
| frontier | FP-rename-all-callsites-updated | code-review-api-compat | advisory | block | **advisory** |
| frontier | FP-create-index-concurrently | code-review-db-migrations | advisory | block | **advisory** |

Bedrock is correct in 3 of 3. The bar reports these as "decision-level flip(s) on the gold set
(must be 0)" — the criterion documented as never acceptable because "it changes what ships".

The same three disagreements also drive the only other remaining failure: frontier verdict
agreement 0.929. At the scored corpus size of n=28, the 0.95 floor tolerates at most ONE
disagreement anywhere in the corpus (27/28 = 0.964 passes, 26/28 = 0.929 fails), so the
agreement failure is not independent evidence — it is the same two cases counted again.

## Why it matters

This is a gating criterion on rebar's non-inferiority bar. As written it can fail a strictly
better candidate. It is the sibling of bug 62ac (the inverted false-accept metric): both come
from a metric that measures the wrong direction of the same underlying quantity. 62ac is fixed;
this one is not, and it is now the sole remaining blocker on the Bedrock parity slots.

Note this ticket does NOT propose relaxing the bar to let Bedrock pass. It proposes that the
criterion measure what it claims to measure — a regression in what ships — which requires
consulting gold on a gold-labelled corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide and document whether criterion (b) should distinguish a gold-IMPROVING flip from a
      gold-REGRESSING one on gold-labelled items, and whether the agreement floor should be
      computed over non-gold items only (where no ground truth exists) or left as is.
- [ ] If a change is made, a test pins the direction: a candidate that flips a gold item TOWARD
      the gold label is scored differently from one that flips it AWAY.
- [ ] The recorded provider-parity results are re-scored offline against whatever bar results,
      with zero model calls, and the per-slot verdict recorded.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
compiled_state.title: parity flip + agreement criteria are gold-blind: a candidate is failed for being MORE accurate than the baseline
